facts.statement: Fossils of Muiscasaurus were discovered in the Paja Formation near Villa de Leyva in the Boyacá Department of Colombia.
facts.quote: The fossils of Muiscasaurus were found in the Paja Formation, whose sediments are exposed near the town of Villa de Leyva in Boyacá Department.

facts.statement: The remains were found in 2010 inside a limestone concretion within the Arcillolitas abigarradas Member.
facts.quote: These remains were found in 2010 in the middle of a limestone concretion, known as the Arcillolitas abigarradas Member

facts.statement: The genus and species Muiscasaurus catheti were formally described in 2015.
facts.quote: These remains were designated in 2015 as the new genus and species Muiscasaurus catheti

facts.statement: The genus name Muiscasaurus honors the Muisca people of central Colombia and the Greek word for reptile.
facts.quote: The genus name being a reference to the Muisca of central Colombia, with the Latinized Greek word saurus, "reptile".

facts.statement: The known fossils represent a juvenile individual based on incomplete bone formation and skull proportions.
facts.quote: The Muiscasaurus fossils corresponds to a juvenile individual, given the incomplete ossification of the vertebrae and the proportions of the skull.

facts.statement: The preserved skull is 45 cm long, with total cranial length estimated between 48 and 65 cm.
facts.quote: Muiscasaurus was a relatively large animal: the preserved skull length is 45 cm, and, depending on its exact proportions, could be between 48 – 65 cm total cranial length.

facts.statement: While the juvenile was about 3 meters long, adults could have reached up to 5 meters in length.
facts.quote: This individual could reach 3 m long and up to 5 m long in adults.

facts.statement: Muiscasaurus had a compact, streamlined body with a half-moon shaped tail and flipper-like limbs.
facts.quote: Like all advanced ichthyosaurs, Muiscasaurus must had a compact and streamlined body, with a tail shaped like a half moon and all four legs transformed into flippers.

facts.statement: Muiscasaurus is distinguished by a very thin premaxilla and a nasal aperture partially divided into two ovals by a spur-shaped process.
facts.quote: Muiscasaurus differs from its closest relatives by a combination of features: it had a very thin premaxilla, the nasal aperture is partially divided in two ovals for a spur-shaped nasal process

facts.statement: Its teeth were very thin and lacked the thick enamel and coarse striations found in similar ichthyosaurs like Pervushovisaurus and Platypterygius.
facts.quote: the teeth were very thin and lacking of the thick enamel and the coarse striations, whereas in similar ichthyosaurs as Pervushovisaurus and Platypterygius had more robust teeth and grooves in the enamel.

facts.statement: Muiscasaurus lived in modern Colombia during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Muiscasaurus is an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur that lived in modern Colombia during the Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Muiscasaurus lived between 125.77 and 113.2 million years ago during the Barremian to Aptian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Muiscasaurus is classified within the family Ophthalmosauridae.
facts.quote: Muiscasaurus was described based on fossils that were classified as belonging to the Ophthalmosauridae family

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis suggests Muiscasaurus occupies a very basal position within the Ophthalmosauridae family.
facts.quote: Muiscasaurus seems particularly occupied a very basal position within the family, with respect to the subgroup composed by Platypterygius, Caypullisaurus and Brachypterygius

facts.statement: Analysis suggests Muiscasaurus was a specialized predator feeding on smaller, softer prey, unlike the generalist diet of its relative Kyhytysuka.
facts.quote: The analysis could indicate that while P. sachicarum probably had a generalist diet, Muiscasaurus was a much more specialized form, feeding on smaller and softer prey items.

facts.statement: The precise age of the specimen was difficult to establish because attached ammonites were too poorly preserved to identify.
facts.quote: Although ammonites were found attached to the fossils, their poor preservation prevented identifying them and thereby establish the stratigraphy and precise age of the specimen.
